Quick update from the account side: Oakmont's traffic is routed through a long-lived VPC peering arrangement with our us-east-1 edge nodes. Their NetOps reports repeated SYN timeouts to our NAT IPs and elevated TCP RTOs starting at 07:50. They also observed DNS lookup latency spikes for oakmont-cdn.net which sits in front of their auth service.

I've attached the connection logs they sent (connection_logs_us-east1.txt). They're asking for:

- A short mitigation plan they can share with their Ops and CTO (they're sensitive about callouts to their customers)
- ETA for a fix or a safe fallback plan (e.g., routing to another region or flipping to a different peering path)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High error rate + p95 latency on inference calls since 07:55 (Oakmont Checkout)

Diagnosed root cause (initial):

- Observed intermittent BGP flaps on the peering path between our us-east-1 edge routers and Oakmont's VPC edge (AS64512 <-> AS43900). Flaps correlate with connection resets in the first 20m of the incident.
- Simultaneous spike in DNS A-record lookup latency for oakmont-cdn.net (~700–1200ms) from our edge nodes; many client connections timed out waiting on name resolution.
- Their firewall/NAT on the customer side hit connection-tracking limits causing asymmetric TCP resets; NAT stats attached (nat_stats_snapshot.json).

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00 ET):
- Temporarily increased conntrack limits and rebalanced NAT mappings for the affected peering; error rate dropped from ~30% -> ~4% in 20 minutes.
- Added a conditional route to fail traffic over an alternate peering path and enabled forced DNS caching for the Oakmont hostnames at our edge for 60s TTL.

Current status: 5xxs down to ~4%, p95 latency improved but still ~1.8x baseline on some paths. We've scheduled a targeted peering handshake with the transit provider and Oakmont NetOps at 11:30 ET.

Next steps (RCA track):
- Investigate the underlying cause of the BGP flaps with transit provider (logs, recent policy changes).
- Recommend long-term: increase customer NAT conntrack capacity or use SNAT pooling on their side; consider dedicated peering for payment-critical flows.
- Draft RCA and timeline for Oakmont leadership; Jordan/Marissa to coordinate the exec note.

Technical artifacts attached: connection_logs_us-east1.txt, nat_stats_snapshot.json.

— Olga Petrov
Sr. SRE, Network Reliability
Redwood Inference
